question: Could an independent PrefScope concept audit reveal actionable coverage gaps or unwanted behavior patterns in the released EuroMultiSynth-Instruct data, beyond synthgen's judge score and deduplication?
facts: OpenEuroLLM/Taskboard#437 describes generation, judge filtering and same-language near-duplicate removal for multilingual instruction data.
The public synthgen run report documents 4,160,598 released rows in 35 languages after quality filtering and near-duplicate removal.
The PrefScope project associated with OpenEuroLLM/Taskboard#353 can ingest single prompt/response rows, retain language metadata and compute concept-feature statistics.
PrefScope feature names and activations are hypotheses; numerical correlation is not proof of semantic meaning or causal data quality.
unknowns: Whether PrefScope has already been applied to EuroMultiSynth-Instruct by the project team or in private discussions.
Whether the chosen embedding/lens works comparably across selected low-resource languages.
Whether discovered concept gaps predict real downstream model-quality improvements rather than sampling artifacts.
Actual execution cost, compatible exact dataset schema and available evaluation benchmarks.

experiment_proposal.intervention: Offline post-hoc audit only; no retraining and no automatic contact.
experiment_proposal.minimum_test: Check actual dataset schema; sample fixed-seed prompts/responses within 4 languages (2 high-resource, 2 low-resource), record exact dataset revision, and run PrefScope feature summaries.
experiment_proposal.comparator: Existing language-specific judge scores and near-duplicate statistics on the same held-out sample; include hand-labeled control examples.
experiment_proposal.falsification: Stop if concepts are dominated by language artifacts, fail held-out validation, or reveal no stable gap beyond baseline.
experiment_proposal.decision_owner: OpenEuroLLM maintainers; not established that they have not already coordinated
